questions.q: What is a 'collision,' as Preview flags it?
options: The target's version of a customization differs from the Update Set's version
An Update Set file that fails to upload
Two users logged into the same instance at once
A Business Rule that runs twice on the same record
questions.explain: A collision happens when the target's current version of something differs from what's in the Update Set, usually from a direct edit on the target.

questions.q: What usually causes a collision in the first place?
options: A network timeout during export
Someone editing the same customization directly on the target instance, outside the Update Set
The Update Set being too large to preview
The source instance being in maintenance mode
questions.explain: Collisions are a natural consequence of two people (or Update Sets) touching the same configuration independently.

options: An Update Set references something, like a Script Include, that doesn't exist yet on the target instance
A field that was deleted from the dictionary
An ACL that grants too much access
A Business Rule with no condition script
questions.explain: This happens when the referenced piece lives in a different, not-yet-applied Update Set -- committing dependency order correctly prevents it.

questions.q: What is the real fix for a flagged collision?
options: Always keep the target instance's version automatically
Always keep the Update Set's version automatically
Review both versions side by side and deliberately choose which one to keep
Delete the customization entirely from both instances
questions.explain: A collision needs a deliberate decision between the two versions -- never letting either side win by default.

questions.q: What is a 'skipped' record, and who causes it?
options: A record ServiceNow automatically deletes after 90 days
A specific flagged change an administrator deliberately chose not to apply during Preview
A change that failed to export due to a file size limit
A record that was never captured in any Update Set
questions.explain: Unlike collisions or missing dependencies, a skip is a deliberate administrator choice during Preview, not something ServiceNow detects automatically.
